title: Evaluation map from the injective bar total to the cyclic total
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site in a universe containing all parameter sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules $\mathcal M_R$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and action categories $\mathcal A_P(R)$ for the condensed group $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $H$ be profinite, $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$ continuous, $\tau=u(1)$, and take the regular module $R$ with trivial $H$-action. Fix any nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $a:R[0]\to I^\bullet$. Write $U$ for full action-forgetting, $V$ for restriction along $u$, $\Gamma_H$ for the invariant submodule functor and $Q$ for ordinary derived localization. Let $T$ act on $VI$ by $1\in\mathbf Z$, equivalently by $\tau$ on $I$. On the compatible bar model of [lem-sfb-internal-bar-roof-adjunction], put
$$D^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline H^p],UI^q),\qquad d_{\mathrm{Tot}}=d_h+(-1)^p d_I\quad(p,q\geq0).$$
Here $d_h$ is the action-dependent inhomogeneous differential. Let $b_H:\Gamma_H I\to\operatorname{Tot}D$ be invariant inclusion, $V_R^p=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline H^p],R)$, and let $j:QV_R\to Q\operatorname{Tot}D$ be the map induced by $a$ in resolution degree zero. Identify $\eta:R\Gamma_H(R[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Tot}D$ with $Q(b_H)$ using the normalized resolution comparison.

Let $K(VI)^n=UI^n\oplus UI^{n-1}$ with differential $(dx,(T-1)x-dy)$. There is a cochain map $E:\operatorname{Tot}D\to K(VI)$ whose components are identity for $p=0$, evaluation at $\tau$ for $p=1$, and zero for $p\geq2$. Evaluation is precomposition with $R\to R[\underline H]$, $1\mapsto[\tau]$, on every profinite base change. It satisfies
$$(d_hm)(\tau)=\tau m-m,\qquad Eb_H=(\mathrm{inclusion},0).$$
For $\epsilon:V_R\to[R\xrightarrow0R]$ given by identity, evaluation at $\tau$, and zero in higher degrees, and $k=K(Va):[R\xrightarrow0R]\to K(VI)$, one has the equality of cochain maps $Ej_{\mathrm{rep}}=k\epsilon$, and $k$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Using the mate $\beta$ of [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting] and $\theta=\lambda^{-1}$ with $\theta\alpha=Qb$ (where $\alpha$ is the canonical right-derived computation unit and $b$ the cyclic invariant inclusion) of [lem-sfb-cyclic-row-derived-comparison], their composite $c=\lambda^{-1}\beta$ is represented on this resolution by
$$c=Q(k)^{-1}Q(Eb_H),\qquad c\eta^{-1}j=Q(\epsilon).$$
These equations use the canonical source resolution identification, hold without injectivity of $VI$, and do not assert invertibility of $\beta$ or that the underived bar computes derived invariants.

proof.text: Use the compatible bar data of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. For a profinite base $S$, evaluation sends a natural internal function $f$ to its value on the constant map $S\to H$ with value $\tau$. Equivalently it precomposes internal Hom by the free-module map $R\to R[\underline H]$ sending $1$ to $[\tau]$. Restrictions carry this generator to the same constant generator, so evaluation is an internal $R$-linear map and commutes with every coefficient map, in particular $d_I$. The first and last faces in bar degree zero give $(d_hm)(\tau)=\tau m-m$. These are the face and evaluation rules stated in the cited definition, not an assertion about global-section exactness.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary cyclic calculation, agent-written detail: internal evaluation and degree-zero bar differential

proof.text:
For $z=(z_p)_{p+q=n}$ in the finite-diagonal total, define $E^n(z)=(z_0,\operatorname{ev}_\tau z_1)$, omitting negative-degree terms. The total differential of [def-sp-double-complex-total] gives
$$E^{n+1}(d_{\rm Tot}z)=(d_Iz_0,\operatorname{ev}_\tau(d_hz_0-d_Iz_1))=(d_Iz_0,(T-1)z_0-d_I\operatorname{ev}_\tau z_1)=d_KE^n(z).$$
No column $p\geq2$ can contribute to output column zero or one. Thus this defines the claimed cochain map, including degree zero. Since $b_H$ has only its bar-zero component, its composite with $E$ is exactly $(\mathrm{inclusion},0)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary cyclic calculation, agent-written detail: finite-diagonal calculation with the minus sign in column one

proof.text: Apply the same coordinate calculation to the trivial module $R[0]$: $(T-1)R=0$, so its cyclic total is $[R\xrightarrow0R]$ and its evaluation map is $\epsilon$. The row-zero augmentation $j_{\rm rep}$ postcomposes every internal function by $a^0$. Therefore in degrees zero and one the two composites $Ej_{\rm rep}$ and $k\epsilon$ are respectively $a^0$ and $a^0\operatorname{ev}_\tau=\operatorname{ev}_\tau\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(R[\underline H],a^0)$; both are zero in higher degrees. This proves equality as cochain maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary cyclic calculation, agent-written detail: row-zero coefficient augmentation and evaluation square

proof.text: Restriction is exact by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], hence $Va:R[0]\to VI$ is a bounded-below quasi-isomorphism. The cyclic total preserves such quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-cyclic-total-triangulated], with residual group the trivial profinite group. Consequently $k=K(Va)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $Q(k)$ is invertible. No injectivity statement about $VI$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary cyclic calculation, agent-written detail: valid denominator after restricting the resolution

proof.text:
Put $A=R\Gamma_H(Qa)$, $B=R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}(QVa)$ and $C=Q(k)$. By the injective-resolution computation of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], $\sigma=A^{-1}\alpha_{H,I}:Q\Gamma_H I\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_H(R[0])$ is the canonical source identification. Indeed $A$ is invertible because $Qa$ is invertible and $R\Gamma_H$ is a functor; $\alpha_{H,I}$ is invertible because $I$ is nonnegative termwise injective. Thus $\sigma^{-1}=\alpha_{H,I}^{-1}A$. The mate equation of [lem-sfb-relative-restriction-mate-forgetting] gives $\beta_I\alpha_{H,I}=\alpha_{\mathbf Z,VI}Q(\iota_I)$, with residual group trivial. The comparison of [lem-sfb-cyclic-row-derived-comparison] gives $\theta_{VI}\alpha_{\mathbf Z,VI}=Q(b_{VI})$, even though $VI$ need not be injective. Naturality along $a$ and $Va$ reads $\beta_I A=B\beta_R$ and $\theta_{VI}B=C\theta_R$. Thus, since $c=\theta_R\beta_R$ and $C$ is invertible by step 4,
$$c\sigma=C^{-1}\theta_{VI}\beta_I\alpha_{H,I}=Q(k)^{-1}Q(b_{VI}\iota_I)=Q(k)^{-1}Q(Eb_H).$$
The last equality is step 2: both cochain maps include $H$-invariants into the first coordinate and are zero in the second. This proves the roof formula under $\sigma$ without inverting $\beta$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary cyclic calculation, agent-written detail: derived mate equation and comparison normalization on the restricted complex

proof.text:
The normalized bar model of [lem-sfb-internal-bar-roof-adjunction] says $\eta=Q(b_H)\sigma^{-1}$, with $Q(b_H)$ invertible. In particular $\eta\sigma=Q(b_H)$ and $\eta^{-1}=\sigma Q(b_H)^{-1}$; this fixes the domain of every factor in the cancellation below. Using the roof formula of step 5 and $j=Q(j_{\rm rep})$, cancel this denominator and then use step 3:
$$c\eta^{-1}j=c\sigma Q(b_H)^{-1}Q(j_{\rm rep})=Q(k)^{-1}Q(E)Q(j_{\rm rep})=Q(k)^{-1}Q(k\epsilon)=Q(\epsilon).$$
Only $Q(k)$ and $Q(b_H)$ have been inverted. The argument makes no assertion that $\beta$ or $j$ is invertible.
